properties.name: A cluster can be declared deliberately separate, so disconnected_community reports undeclared islands instead of one permanent warning
properties.statement:
A group of nodes can be declared a DELIBERATE PARTITION — a subsystem that genuinely does not couple to the rest of the design — so `disconnected_community` reports "N declared partitions, 0 undeclared" rather than one standing warning. The value is NOT silencing the finding. It is that a NEW accidental island becomes visible against the declared ones, which today it is not.

=== ⚠️ THE CONDITION THIS IS BUILT UNDER — Anthony, 2026-08-09 ===

He settled `dec:legitimate-islands-need-the-detector-fix` as: "C now, A next with the read-back, not B, not D." THIS REQUIREMENT IS OPTION A, AND IT IS CONDITIONAL.

**THE MARKER MUST BE READ BACK, OR IT MUST NOT BE BUILT.** A report must state, for each declared partition, ITS SIZE AND WHEN IT WAS DECLARED — "declared separate 2026-08-09 at 5 nodes; now 121." A declaration that nothing reads is set once and never revisited, and a partition declared at 5 nodes is still declared at 500 with nobody looking.

WHY THE CONDITION EXISTS RATHER THAN BEING TRUST IN GOOD PRACTICE: `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches` warns IN ITS OWN TEXT that "another marker nothing reads" would be a fourth instance of the very disease it documents — declared vocabulary with no computation behind it. Building A without the read-back would make this design's own recorded warning come true, in the increment that was supposed to answer it. `dec:edge-orthogonality` states the same test as an accepted rule: a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT.

SO THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS NOT "a partition can be declared". It is: **a declared partition's size and age are visible without being asked for**, and a NEW undeclared island is distinguishable from the declared ones at a glance.

=== THE REST OF THE CASE, UNCHANGED ===

THE DEFECT IN THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS THE SUGGESTED FIX, not the finding. `disconnected_community` proposes `generate_bridge` — creating edges to connect the cluster. Where the separation is correct, acting on that suggestion FABRICATES RELATIONSHIPS THAT DO NOT EXIST in order to silence a warning about a separation that is right. That is manufacturing connectivity, and it is the same act as formatting coverage into existence — with the difference that here THE TOOL PROPOSES IT. **That half is now `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` and ships FIRST, independently of this requirement** (option C), because it is a live hazard whether or not partitions are ever declarable.

WHY ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS NOT ENOUGH, which is the part that makes this a mechanism and not a workflow note: `acknowledge_defect` is a one-time answer to a finding whose SIZE keeps changing. Acknowledged at 88 nodes it now reads 121 — at what point is it a different finding? And an alarm that can never be cleared is one everyone learns to skip, so the real disconnection arrives inside a warning nobody reads. **MEASURED HERE, 2026-08-09: the heal id MOVED WITHIN ONE SESSION as the cluster grew 5 → 7 nodes (`heal:33d1548dae64e97a` → `heal:4dc24c4df2dd7aa7`), so an acknowledgement made at 5 would already point at a defect that no longer exists.** That is why option D was rejected.

REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY MET THIS AND WROTE DOWN THE ANSWER. dec:documentation-has-no-operational-coupling (ACCEPTED, 2026-07-24) records the identical situation — three bridges attempted, all refused as lies, the island accepted — and concludes "flagging it is a false positive of the BL-84 family, and THE FIX BELONGS IN THE DETECTOR RATHER THAN IN THE DESIGN." It also states the exact constraint storyflow independently arrived at sixteen days later: "the exemption must not be written in a way that hides a genuine disconnection." **That sentence is also why option B was rejected: an INFERRED exemption is precisely the kind that hides, and an inference cannot be argued with.**

REPRODUCED IN THIS DESIGN WITHIN THE HOUR OF THE REPORT ARRIVING: capturing four governance requirements under dec:governance-integrates-not-splits produced a 5-node disconnected cluster with `generate_bridge` proposed. No honest bridge existed, so none was drawn. Storyflow hit it at 121 nodes; reflow2 hit it at 5. Both clusters are GOVERNANCE, and both GROW as governance is properly captured — so the detector currently penalises exactly the work dec:governance-integrates-not-splits committed to.

SOURCE: storyflow gap D of the peer set — raised by storybug Boss (47accf78), characterised and filed by api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Their stated bound: the growth from 88 to 121 is suggestive, not proven, because the two measurements may not share a scope.
